literal: If asked what is the non-diminishing of wealth, it is requiring the non-coveting of the property in another's hand.
translation: If you ask how to prevent your own wealth from diminishing, the answer is: you must not covet the property that belongs to another.
modern: ஒருவனுடைய செல்வம் குறையாமல் இருப்பதற்கான வழி யாது என்றால், அவன் பிறனுடைய கையில் உள்ள பொருளை விரும்பாமல் இருக்க வேண்டும்.
explanation: This couplet explains the secret to preserving one's own wealth. The author states that if a person wishes for their wealth not to decrease (அஃகாமை), the key is to avoid coveting (வெஃகாமை) the possessions of others (பிறன்கைப்பொருள்). Covetousness leads to ruin and loss of what one already has, whereas contentment and respecting others' property secure one's own prosperity. The wordplay between 'அஃகாமை' (non-diminishing) and 'வெஃகாமை' (non-coveting) beautifully links the action of restraint to the result of preservation.
